title: Evaluation of the effects of the "Patient Education and Training Intervention for Chronic Low Back Pain"
summary:
Many people suffer from recurring and prolonged low back pain. The main reasons for this are too little physical activity and too much mental stress. The "Patient Education and Training Intervention for Chronic Low Back Pain (PATRIC)" was developed to improve the health care of those affected. This programme is aimed at adults (aged 18 and over) with chronic low back pain and comprises seven practical education and training sessions (60-90 minutes each), which are carried out in groups close to home at weekly intervals under expert guidance. The programme focuses on providing important information and skills for coping with low back pain as well as special movement and relaxation exercises.
The study participants are made up of patients from several medical and/or physiotherapy practices. All practices taking part in the study are randomly assigned to one of two groups (either the group of intervention practices or the group of control practices) (randomisation). The patients of the intervention practices participate in the education and training programme, while the patients of the control practices do not. The randomised allocation ensures that the groups are comparable. The probability of being assigned to one of the two groups is the same.
The aim of the scientific study is to investigate how effective this education and training programme is in terms of low back pain and coping with it. To this end, all study participants are asked to take part in a survey on three dates (within eight months). The main hypothesis is that patients who participate in the programme (intervention group) have less severe back pain, less functional impairment and a higher quality of life than patients who do not participate in the programme (control group).
conditions: Chronic non-specific low back pain (with significant functional impairment)

interventions.name: Patient education and training intervention consisting of information transfer, aerobic activities, strengthening exercises, stretching exercises, mobilisation and coordination exercises, relaxation exercises - PMR (7 education and training units of 60-90 minutes each once a week)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Chronic (> 12 weeks) non-specific low back pain (back area below the ribcage and above the gluteal folds) with significant functional impairment (grade II - IV in the Chronic Pain Grade - Patient Questionnaire); in ongoing therapy
Exclusion criteria:
Chronic low back pain due to the following specific causes: Tumour in the area of the spine; infection in the area of the spine; vertebral fractures that are not stably penetrated; autoimmune, inflammatory rheumatic diseases; symptomatic radiculopathy; cauda syndrome.
Further exclusion criteria: Recognition of low back pain as an occupational disease (in accordance with the German Ordinance on Occupational Diseases); planned, applied for or ongoing rehabilitation procedure due to low back pain.
